story.learningGoal: Compare access to savings, early withdrawal and selling investments.
story.talkTo: Who would you like to hear from?
story.arrivalSetting: A Hyderabad lane. A small home. You’re helping this fictional family look after its money.
story.arrivalDialogue: I’m Gullu, the family’s living gullak. Today, you get to help us make a difficult choice.
story.householdSetting: Tap a name to hear what matters to them.

dialogue.nani: I’ve kept some savings in a fixed deposit. That money has a job: looking after me later.
dialogue.amma: My tiffin orders help with everyday expenses. We also keep money aside for surprises.
dialogue.gullu: Some money is easy to reach. Some is put away for later. Let’s look before we decide.

story.moneySetting: These are starting balances for this story, not your personal portfolio.
story.moneyDialogue: The emergency savings are ready to use. The other pots have different trade-offs.
story.reserveNote: This reserve is separate from the family’s everyday spending.
story.fdNote: Closing early may reduce interest. The actual terms matter.
story.marketNote: Its value can change. Selling means fewer units remain invested.
story.assumptions: Illustrative scenario fixtures: starting balances are assumed, not bank quotes. Outcomes show immediate trade-offs only; no fees, interest or future prices are calculated.
story.billDescription: Nani needs hospital treatment. The family has an unexpected bill to pay this week.
story.billDialogue: The bill is {bill}. We can pay from different pots, but each choice changes what we have left.

emergency.label: Use the emergency savings
emergency.description: Pay the bill from money kept ready for surprises.
emergency.consequence: The bill is paid from the emergency reserve. Nani’s fixed deposit and investment are untouched.
emergency.learning: A reserve can make an unexpected expense easier to handle.
emergency.tradeoff: There is less ready cash for the next surprise. The family will need a plan to rebuild it.
emergency.reaction: We used the buffer. What would we do if another bill arrived?

fd.label: Close Nani’s fixed deposit early
fd.description: Use the deposit to pay, keeping the emergency reserve available.
fd.consequence: The family pays the bill by closing the fixed deposit early. The emergency reserve stays available.
fd.delta: The ₹15,000 bill is funded from the deposit. Remaining proceeds depend on its withdrawal terms; they are not calculated here.
fd.learning: Money put away for later may still be accessible, with conditions.
fd.tradeoff: Early closure may reduce interest and interrupt the deposit’s plan. Check the terms before comparing costs.
fd.reaction: The bill is covered. What did the family give up by closing early?

market.label: Sell part of the investment
market.description: Sell enough units to pay, keeping the reserve and deposit.
market.consequence: The family pays the bill by selling part of its fictional investment. The reserve and deposit remain.
market.delta: Units are sold to fund the ₹15,000 bill. Prices, settlement, fees and the remaining holding are not calculated here.
market.learning: Investments have changing values and may take time to turn into spendable cash.
market.tradeoff: Fewer units remain invested. A future rise or fall affects what is left; nobody knows which comes next.
market.reaction: We kept the reserve. How does selling change the family’s future flexibility?

story.uncertainty: Nobody knows tomorrow’s prices or the next family expense. These alternatives explore flexibility, not a winning investment.
story.consequenceTitle: The bill is paid. Here’s what changed.
story.reflectionSetting: There is no score for picking the biggest return. Think about being ready for a surprise.
story.reflectionDialogue: Thank you for thinking it through with us. What would you explain to someone at home?
story.reflectionPrompt: What matters most when an unexpected bill arrives?

reserve.label: Having some money easy to reach
reserve.feedback: Yes—ready savings can reduce the need to interrupt another money plan. Rebuilding the reserve matters too.

terms.label: Checking the conditions before withdrawing
terms.feedback: Yes—access, timing and early-withdrawal terms change a decision. A balance alone doesn’t tell the whole story.

uncertainty.label: Remembering that future prices are unknown
uncertainty.feedback: Yes—a later price cannot tell us what the family knew that day. Compare choices using the needs and information they had.

story.takeHome: Try this at home: explain the difference between money for everyday needs and an emergency reserve. You don’t need to share any real balances.

tips.newWelcome: Namaste! I'm Gullu, Nani's gullak. Press Play and we'll run her first errand at the kirana together.
tips.newPlayMoney: Everything here is play money, so mistakes cost nothing. Try a choice, see what happens, try again.

tips.quizRetry: Your last quick check isn't passed yet, and that's okay. Read the lesson once more and try again.
tips.habit: Small and regular beats big and rare. ₹10 every week fills me faster than you'd think.
tips.gulluGrow: I grow when you save regularly and spot scams, never when you get lucky.
tips.gulluKintsugi: I broke once, and Nani mended me with gold. Mistakes can be mended too.
tips.portfolioPaper: This portfolio is paper only. Watch how your choices change it; no real money moves.

world.candy-economy: At the kirana, compare the price per toffee, not just the price on the packet.
world.savings-quest: Before you spend, ask: is this a need or a want? A want can wait a week.
world.bankopolis: A bank keeps money safe and pays a little interest. Never share your UPI PIN or OTP with anyone.
world.market-mayhem: If someone promises to double your money in a week, it's a trick. Ask Nani before you believe it.
world.grow-your-money: Money left to grow earns on what it already earned. Starting early matters more than starting big.
world.stock-street: Prices go up and down every day. A company's report card tells you more than one day's price.
world.life-simulator: Life brings surprise bills. Money kept aside for emergencies means you never have to sell in a hurry.
world.finance-tycoon: Every plan needs a goal, a time and an amount. Write down all three before you begin.

xp.name: XP
xp.definition: Experience points you earn by finishing lessons and missions. They show effort; they are not money and cannot buy anything.

mastery.name: Mastery
mastery.definition: Gullak's estimate of how well you know an idea, based on your quiz answers. It rises and falls as you learn; it is not a mark.

habitScore.name: Habit score
habitScore.definition: How regularly you practise good money habits, like saving and spotting scams. It never measures how much money you made.

playMoney.name: Play money
playMoney.definition: Pretend rupees and coins for practice. Nothing in Gullak can be spent, withdrawn or lost in real life.

portfolio.name: Portfolio
portfolio.definition: Everything you own, in one place: cash, savings and investments. Yours is a paper portfolio of pretend money.

interest.name: Interest
interest.definition: Money a bank pays you for keeping your savings with it, or money you pay when you borrow.

inflation.name: Inflation
inflation.definition: Prices slowly rising over time, so the same ₹100 buys a little less each year. A samosa that once cost ₹10 may cost ₹15 now.

sip.name: SIP
sip.definition: Systematic investment plan: putting the same small amount into a mutual fund every month, like a monthly gullak habit.

nav.name: NAV
nav.definition: Net asset value: the price of one unit of a mutual fund, worked out once a day from everything the fund holds.

daysPractised.name: Days practised
daysPractised.definition: Every distinct day you practise counts. Breaks never reduce this total.

previousClose.name: Previous close
previousClose.definition: The last price when the market closed on the previous trading day. Today's change is measured from it.

dayRange.name: Day's range
dayRange.definition: The lowest and highest prices traded today. A wide range means the price moved a lot in one day.

week52Range.name: 52-week range
week52Range.definition: The lowest and highest prices in the past year. It shows how far the price can swing, not where it will go next.

volume.name: Volume
volume.definition: How many shares or units changed hands today. High volume means many people were buying and selling.

oneYearChange.name: 1-year change
oneYearChange.definition: How much the price moved since about a year ago. Past moves never promise future ones.

indexPoints.name: Index points
indexPoints.definition: An index is measured in points, not rupees. It tracks a group of companies, so it rises when most of them rise.

stock.name: Stock
stock.definition: A tiny slice of one company. Its price moves with how people judge that company's future.

etf.name: ETF
etf.definition: Exchange-traded fund: a basket, often copying an index, that trades on the stock exchange like a share.

mutualFund.name: Mutual fund
mutualFund.definition: A pool of many people's money that a fund manager invests. You own units, priced once a day by NAV.

fundCategory.name: Fund category
fundCategory.definition: SEBI sorts every mutual fund into a category, such as large cap or liquid, so funds of one kind can be compared.

page.title: How Gullak works
page.intro: Gullak teaches money by letting you try it. Here is everything you need to know, in two minutes.
page.loopLearnBody: Each lesson takes 3 to 5 minutes. You make choices and see what happens.
page.loopCheckBody: A few questions show what stuck. You can try again as many times as you like.
page.loopUnlockBody: Passing the quick check opens the next lesson on your map.
page.moneyBody: Every rupee, coin and portfolio in Gullak is play money. Nothing can be spent, withdrawn or lost. Growth numbers are assumptions for learning, not promises, and Gullak never tells anyone to buy or sell anything real.
page.gulluBody: Gullu is Nani's mended clay gullak and your guide. Tap Gullu for a tip that fits where you are. Gullu explains ideas; Gullu never gives advice to buy or sell.
page.languageBody: Use the language menu at the top of the screen. You can switch between English, हिन्दी and తెలుగు at any time, and your progress stays the same.
page.offlineBody: Install Gullak from your browser menu to open it like an app. Pages you have already opened can keep working when the internet drops.
page.privacyBody: Your profile and progress are saved only on this device. If you share the phone, use “{reset}” on the Me page before handing it over.
page.glossaryIntro: Look for the small question mark next to these words anywhere in Gullak.
